questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used. questions.questionText: A student intends to measure accurately the diameter of a wire (known to be approximately 1mm) and the internal diameter of a pipe (known to be approximately 2cm). What are the most appropriate instruments for the student to use to make these measurements? wire pipe

The power P dissipated in a resistor of resistance R is calculated using the expression V2 P = R where V is the potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor. The percentage uncertainty in V is 5% and in R is 2%. What is the percentage uncertainty in P?

options.A: A body remains at constant velocity unless acted upon by a resultant force.
options.B: A satellite in circular motion about the Earth has a constant velocity.
options.C: A water drop leaving a spinning umbrella travels at a constant velocity.

questions.questionText: A resultant force causes an object to accelerate. What is equal to the resultant force?

options.A: the acceleration of the object per unit mass
options.B: the change in kinetic energy of the object per unit time
options.C: the change in momentum of the object per unit time
options.D: the change in velocity of the object per unit time
